date.quote: In this writ petition, the Petitioner has challenged the Show Cause Notice No.03/2022-GST dated 11.07.2022 issued by the Respondent herein.

events.quote: The specific case of the Petitioner is that the Petitioner was issued with a notice in Form DRC-01A dated 23.06.2022 by the Respondent, directing the Petitioner to pay the demanded tax amount along with applicable interest and penalty under Section 74(5) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as “CGST Act”) by 01.07.2022.
In response to the said notice in Form DRC-01A dated 23.06.2022, the Petitioner sent its detailed Reply dated 05.07.2022.

However, without considering the Petitioner's reply, the Respondent has issued the impugned Show Cause Notice dated 11.07.2022 to the Petitioner demanding the aforesaid amount as tax due from the Petitioner.

defects_argued.quote: In response to the said notice in Form DRC-01A dated 23.06.2022, the Petitioner sent its detailed Reply dated 05.07.2022.

outcome.quote: Accordingly, this Writ Petition is dismissed.

review.notes:
The scope test requires (1) a GST demand under s.73/74, and (2) the court ruling on, or being asked to rule on, a procedural complaint.

Condition (1) fails in substance: the petition challenges only a Show Cause Notice dated 11.07.2022 proposing demands under Section 74(1) (Para 2) — not a confirmed demand order. No adjudication/assessment order exists yet; the matter is still at the SCN stage.

Condition (2) also fails as actually applied: although the petitioner did raise a procedural complaint — that the SCN was issued “without considering the Petitioner’s reply” to the prior DRC-01A (Para 4) — the Court never rules on that complaint’s merits. Instead, it dismisses the petition outright as premature/not maintainable under Article 226 (Para 7–8), holding that challenging a SCN before adjudication is impermissible, and merely grants liberty to file a reply with a future personal hearing. This is a threshold maintainability dismissal, not a ruling on the procedural complaint itself.
